Q1: The Tier Profile for p-Xylene indicates known, significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental (ENV), inhalation (IHL), and oral (ORL) exposures, as well as organ and systemic hazards (OGN). Dermal and eye hazards (SKN) are classified at Tier 2, suggesting potential risks identified through a broader data perspective. Data on its endocrine disruption potential (EDC) is currently deficient, placing it at Tier 4 for this class.
Q2: p-Xylene is identified on several important "Lists of Concern." It is included on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor, and is also recognized under the U.S. Clean Water Act and as a Hazardous Air Pollutant, reflecting its environmental regulatory status.
Q3: p-Xylene is extensively characterized, evidenced by its 45,000 literature references, which is significantly higher than the typical median. Its precise molecular formula (C8H10), classification as a "Small Molecule," and absence of UVCB status further confirm its well-defined nature, with only one hazard class (endocrine disruption) currently lacking sufficient data.
